Ashland Inc. is an American chemical company based in Wilmington, Delaware. Founded in 1924 as Ashland Refining Company, it has evolved from a regional petroleum refiner into a diversified industrial conglomerate. The company has undergone significant transformations, including a major diversification strategy in the 1960s and a merger with Marathon Oil in 1998, which marked a shift away from traditional oil refining.

Ashland operates through five divisions: Chemical Intermediates and Solvents, Composites, Industrial Specialties, Personal and Home Care, and Pharmaceuticals, Food and Beverage, and Agriculture. It is a leading provider of petroleum, chemical, and highway construction products, with notable offerings including Valvoline motor oil and car-care products. With around 25,000 employees and annual revenues nearing $8 billion, Ashland has a strong global presence, serving customers in over 140 countries, primarily in the transportation and construction sectors.

Atkore is committed to operational efficiency, quality, and safety, ensuring it meets the needs of its clients effectively.

BioLife Plasma Services is a prominent global plasma collection company and a subsidiary of Takeda. With over 260 donation centers in the U.S. and Europe, BioLife specializes in collecting high-quality plasma used in lifesaving therapies for rare and chronic diseases. The company has more than 80 years of experience in the industry and is recognized as one of the top three plasma organizations worldwide.

BioLife's core service is plasma donation through plasmapheresis, where eligible donors undergo thorough screenings to ensure safety and product quality. The company emphasizes patient-centric innovation and donor safety, rewarding donors for their contributions. BioLife's operations support the production of plasma-derived therapies that treat various conditions, including immunodeficiencies and neuroimmunology. By prioritizing service to donors and patients, BioLife aims to meet the growing global demand for these essential therapies.

Bruker Corporation is an American manufacturer based in Billerica, Massachusetts, specializing in high-performance scientific instruments and analytical solutions. Founded in 1960 in Germany, Bruker initially focused on Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) and Electron Magnetic Resonance (EMR) spectroscopy equipment. Over the years, the company has expanded its offerings to include mass spectrometry, optical spectroscopy, X-ray systems, and MRI solutions, catering to molecular and materials research, life sciences, and industrial applications.

Bruker emphasizes innovation in analytics, supporting advancements in various fields such as cell biology, preclinical imaging, and clinical microbiology. The company collaborates with prestigious institutions like Yale University and the Max Planck Institute, showcasing its commitment to driving research and development. With over 11,000 employees and a presence in more than 90 locations worldwide, Bruker continues to enable breakthroughs in science and industry through its advanced analytical tools and customer support services.

The company is committed to sustainability, with many of its farms certified by the Rainforest Alliance's Better Banana Project.

The company is committed to environmental sustainability and ethical governance, ensuring high food safety standards.

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is a United States government agency dedicated to the nation's civilian space program and aeronautics research. NASA's mission includes exploring space, conducting scientific research, and developing technologies to enhance human understanding and capabilities in air and space.

NASA operates a variety of space missions and programs, including the International Space Station (ISS) and Artemis lunar missions. The agency manages satellites, space telescopes, and robotic spacecraft, while also providing Earth observation data. Its services encompass facility management, logistics, mission coordination, and post-mission analysis. NASA produces a wide range of scientific data products related to Earth observation, which are utilized for research and environmental monitoring.

NASA serves diverse stakeholders, including U.S. government agencies, the scientific community, commercial aerospace companies, educational institutions, and the general public. Its work supports various initiatives in environmental monitoring, climate research, and technological innovation.

ENFRA specializes in flexible EaaS agreements, offering services such as energy optimization, engineering and construction for energy projects, maintenance and asset management, and renewable energy solutions. The company serves mission-critical institutions, including healthcare systems, universities, and manufacturing operations. ENFRA is committed to sustainability, achieving carbon neutrality and aiming for net zero emissions by 2050. Its projects have significantly reduced carbon emissions and saved substantial amounts of natural gas and water.

The company specializes in nuclear components, fuel, reactors, and related services for government, commercial, and medical applications. BWXT has a rich history dating back to 1867 and has evolved significantly, particularly in the nuclear sector since the 1950s.

BWXT designs and manufactures a variety of nuclear products, including naval nuclear components for U.S. Navy submarines and aircraft carriers, nuclear steam generators, and reactor components. The company also produces medical isotopes and radiopharmaceuticals through its subsidiary, BWXT ITG Canada. Additionally, BWXT is involved in government site management for environmental restoration and has developed small modular reactors. Its business units include BWXT Nuclear Energy, Inc. and BWXT Canada, which focus on different aspects of nuclear manufacturing and services.

Calavo Growers, Inc. is a global fresh produce and food distribution company based in Santa Paula, California. Founded in 1924, it began as a cooperative for avocado growers and transitioned to a for-profit corporation in 2001. With over 2,500 employees, Calavo is a leader in the fresh food supply chain, focusing on avocado distribution and marketing, as well as a variety of other fresh produce.

The company operates through three main segments: Fresh Products, which includes avocado distribution and other fresh vegetables; Calavo Foods, which produces value-added avocado products like guacamole and salsa; and Renaissance Food Group, specializing in prepared fresh foods such as salads and sandwiches. Calavo's extensive product portfolio features fresh avocados, prepared avocado products, fresh-cut fruits and vegetables, and ready-to-eat meals. With operations in the U.S., Mexico, Central America, and Chile, Calavo maintains a strong market presence and a commitment to quality and innovation in the food industry.

Consolidated Edison, Inc. (Con Edison) is a leading energy company in the United States, providing electric, gas, and steam services to around 10 million people in New York City and Westchester County. Founded in 1823, Con Edison has a rich history of innovation and growth, evolving from its origins in gas street lighting to operating one of the world's largest energy delivery systems.

The company delivers three main services: electric, gas, and steam. It serves 3.6 million electric customers across a complex network, distributes natural gas to 1.1 million customers, and operates the largest district steam system in the U.S., catering to approximately 1,600 customers in Manhattan. Con Edison is committed to sustainability, aiming for 100% clean energy by 2040, and emphasizes safety, ethics, and customer control in its operations. With annual revenues of about $15 billion and assets totaling $72 billion, Con Edison plays a significant role in the economic landscape of New York.

The company supplies electricity, natural gas, and sustainable energy solutions to around two million customers, including homes, businesses, and public sector entities across the country. With a diverse generation fleet that includes nuclear, hydro, wind, and solar facilities, Constellation has a capacity of over 32,400 megawatts, contributing about 10% of the U.S. grid's clean power.

Founded in 1999, Constellation has evolved through mergers and spinoffs, most recently becoming an independent entity in 2022. The company offers a range of customizable energy products and services, including electricity and natural gas supply, renewable energy solutions, and energy management strategies. Constellation is committed to supporting climate goals and helping customers achieve energy efficiency and decarbonization targets. It serves a wide array of clients, including a significant portion of Fortune 100 companies, and operates in competitive energy markets across multiple states.

The company specializes in the construction, repair, modernization, and maintenance of naval and commercial vessels. As a subsidiary of J.D. Founded in 1882, Irving Shipbuilding has a rich history that includes building significant naval vessels for the Royal Canadian Navy, such as Halifax-class frigates and Arctic and Offshore Patrol Ships. With a workforce of over 16,000 employees, Irving Shipbuilding plays a vital role in Canada's defense supply chain and is a key partner for the Royal Canadian Navy and the Canadian Coast Guard.

The company operates with a focus on quality winemaking and sustainable viticulture practices. Jackson Family Wines boasts an extensive portfolio of 40 wine brands and wineries sourced from vineyards across the globe, including notable regions in the United States, France, Italy, Australia, Chile, South Africa, and Canada. Its flagship product, Kendall-Jackson Vintner's Reserve Chardonnay, has been a top-selling Chardonnay in America for over 30 years. Each winery within the portfolio operates independently, allowing for unique styles and varietal focuses that reflect their specific terroirs.

The company also engages in property development and offers services in aviation, marine transportation, and wastewater treatment. Ledcor is committed to health, safety, and environmental protection, supported by award-winning safety programs.

Northgate González Market, also known as Northgate Market, is a family-owned Hispanic supermarket chain founded in 1980 by Don Miguel González and his family. The company specializes in authentic Mexican grocery products and fresh foods, creating a cultural market experience across Southern California. With a strong presence in five counties, Northgate operates 43-44 locations and employs between 6,000 and 7,500 associates, generating approximately $1 billion in annual sales.

The stores offer a vibrant atmosphere reminiscent of traditional Mexican mercados, featuring fresh produce, meats, and unique specialties. Northgate has also introduced Mercado González, open-air market-style stores that provide a variety of prepared foods. In addition to grocery offerings, the company is involved in real estate, property management, financial services, and medical clinics. Northgate continues to expand its reach and enhance its community focus, making it one of the largest Hispanic supermarket chains in the U.S.

Parker Hannifin Corporation is a global leader in motion and control technologies, founded in 1917 in Cleveland, Ohio. Originally known as the Parker Appliance Company, it has evolved significantly over the years, particularly during World War II when it became a key supplier for the U.S. Air Force. The company adopted its current name after acquiring Hannifin Corporation in 1957 and has since expanded its operations worldwide, with over 300 facilities and nearly 58,000 employees.

Parker designs, manufactures, and distributes engineered components and systems for motion control and fluid management. Its product offerings include valves, fluid connectors, hydraulic and pneumatic cylinders, and filtration technologies. These products serve a wide range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, oil and gas, and life sciences. Parker's innovations have played a role in significant historical events, such as the Spirit of St. Louis and Apollo 11 missions, showcasing its long-standing commitment to enhancing productivity across various sectors.

Nestlé Purina PetCare Company, known as Purina, is a leading American pet food manufacturer based in St. Louis, Missouri. As a subsidiary of Nestlé, it is the largest pet food company in the United States and the second-largest globally. Purina has a rich history dating back to 1894, originally focused on farm animal feed, and has evolved into a prominent player in the pet care industry after its acquisition by Nestlé in 2001.

Purina offers a wide range of pet food brands, including Purina Pro Plan, Dog Chow, Friskies, and Beneful, along with products such as dry and wet dog food, cat food, pet treats, and litter. The company is recognized for its commitment to innovation in pet nutrition, having introduced several pioneering products and research initiatives over the years. Purina caters to various pet owner demographics, providing options for those seeking premium ingredients, fitness-focused diets, and solutions for pets with food allergies.

RailWorks Corporation is a prominent North American provider of rail infrastructure services, focusing on construction, maintenance, repair, and related products for rail and transit systems in the U.S. and Canada. Established in 1998, the company has grown through strategic acquisitions and now operates from its headquarters in New York City, with over 30 offices across 48 states and five Canadian provinces. RailWorks employs around 1,465 people and generates approximately $932.5 million in revenue.

The company offers a wide range of services, including railway construction and rehabilitation, repair and maintenance, and electrical and systems integration. RailWorks is known for its expertise in building and restoring track infrastructure, as well as providing advanced communications systems and traction power for transit operations. Through its subsidiaries, such as L.K. Comstock and NARSTCO, RailWorks also provides durable, recycled-steel products for rail applications. The company serves a diverse clientele, including major transit authorities, transportation agencies, and railroads, contributing to significant projects valued over $3 billion.

Reddy Ice is the leading manufacturer and distributor of packaged ice products in the United States and North America, based in Dallas, Texas. The company has a rich history, originating from the Southland Ice Company founded in 1927. Reddy Ice was established in 1972 and has grown to produce approximately 1.8 million tons of ice annually, serving around 82,000 customer locations across 31 states.

The company offers a diverse range of ice products, including premium cubed ice, block ice, dry ice, gourmet ice, craft ice (notably the IceBlox line launched in 2021), and crushed ice. Reddy Ice emphasizes high industry standards in manufacturing and utilizes advanced logistics for reliable delivery. Additionally, it provides on-site production through its proprietary Ice Factory™ technology and has expanded into hydration services following its acquisition of Baytown Ice in 2024. Reddy Ice serves various sectors, including retail, airlines, construction, and emergency services, ensuring a consistent supply of ice products nationwide.

The J.R. Simplot Company, commonly known as Simplot Company, is a family-owned international food and agriculture business founded in 1929 in Declo, Idaho. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho, it operates across the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Australia, Argentina, and China, employing between 15,000 and 18,000 people. The company emphasizes vertical integration in farming, ranching, food processing, phosphate mining, and fertilizer manufacturing, driven by core values of innovation and respect for resources.

Simplot is a leading player in food processing, being the world's largest frozen potato processor, producing over 3 billion pounds of french fries and potato products annually. Its agriculture division includes phosphate mining and fertilizer manufacturing, supporting millions of crop acres. The company also engages in livestock production and offers animal feed solutions. With a commitment to sustainable practices, Simplot continues to innovate in plant nutrition and ecosystem sustainability to meet the needs of a growing global population.

Teichert, Inc. is a family-owned construction company based in Sacramento, California, founded in 1887. With over 137 years of experience, it operates primarily in California and Nevada as an infrastructure and site development contractor and construction materials producer. The company holds California State Contractor’s License #8, the oldest active license in the state, and has played a significant role in major infrastructure projects, including highways, dams, and airports.

Teichert Construction specializes in mass grading, asphalt paving, concrete work, and heavy civil infrastructure projects. Its services support commercial, industrial, and public works developments. Through Teichert Materials, the company produces a variety of construction materials, including crushed stone, sand, gravel, and ready-mixed concrete. Teichert has a rich history of contributing to significant projects, such as the construction of the North Fork Dam and the expansion of Interstate 80 for the 1960 Winter Olympics. Today, it continues to emphasize quality, safety, and community involvement under the leadership of CEO Mary Teichert.

Toyota Motor Corporation is a leading Japanese automotive manufacturer, established in 1937. It has grown to become the world's largest automobile manufacturer by volume. The company originated from Toyoda Automatic Loom Works and launched its first passenger car, the Model AA, in 1936. Over the years, Toyota has introduced several iconic models, including the Corolla, which is recognized as the world's best-selling car.

Toyota produces a diverse range of vehicles, focusing on reliability, fuel efficiency, and innovation. Its lineup includes popular passenger cars like the Corolla and Prius, as well as SUVs and trucks such as the Land Cruiser and Tundra. The company also offers luxury vehicles under the Lexus brand, which was launched in 1989. Toyota operates manufacturing plants globally, including in the U.S., Europe, and Asia, and provides financial services through its subsidiary, Toyota Motor Credit Corp. The company serves a wide array of markets, targeting individual consumers, fleets, and motorsport enthusiasts across more than 140 countries.

USF is committed to redefining higher education and making a significant impact through its diverse academic offerings and research initiatives.

Biogen is a prominent biotechnology company founded in 1978, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company focuses on developing innovative therapies for neurological, rare, and other serious diseases. Biogen originated in Geneva, Switzerland, and has a rich history of scientific achievement, having been established by notable scientists, including Nobel laureates. It became one of the oldest independent biotech firms in the U.S. after relocating in the early 1980s.

Biogen has a strong portfolio of products, including Avonex for multiple sclerosis and other therapies for conditions like cancer and hemophilia. Interface serves a wide range of commercial sectors, including offices, education, healthcare, and hospitality, with a strong presence in over 100 countries.

ITT Inc. emphasizes technological leadership and customized solutions to address complex challenges and improve efficiency for its customers.

J.D. Irving, Limited (JDI) is a family-owned Canadian conglomerate founded in 1882, with a diverse portfolio that includes forestry, pulp and paper, shipbuilding, transportation, logistics, and oil refining. The company operates primarily in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Maine. JDI has a strong commitment to sustainability, having planted over one billion trees since 1957 and managing an extensive forest plan that emphasizes habitat conservation and carbon stocks.

The company operates through various subsidiaries, focusing on sustainable forestry and wood products, shipbuilding, and logistics services. JDI's shipbuilding division includes yards in Halifax, Liverpool, Shelburne, and Georgetown, specializing in tugboats and fishing trawlers. In transportation, JDI is a leading provider of road and rail services for forest products, ensuring efficient supply chain management. Additionally, JDI's oil division operates the largest refinery in Canada, located in Saint John, which processes over 300,000 barrels of oil per day.

The company has delivered over 690,000 homes and operates in 49 markets across nine states, with a focus on personalized, built-to-order single-family homes. It emphasizes affordability, energy efficiency, and customization, allowing buyers to select features through its design studios.

KB Home is known for its commitment to sustainability, offering ENERGY STAR certified homes, WaterSense-labeled homes, and solar-powered communities. As a publicly traded company on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker KBH, KB Home reported $6.93 billion in revenues for 2024.

Appleton International Airport (ATW) is a mid-sized commercial airport located in Greenville, Wisconsin, about 3 nautical miles from Appleton. It is the third largest airport in the state and serves as a key gateway for Northeast Wisconsin. Formerly known as Outagamie County Regional Airport, ATW offers nonstop flights to 23 destinations through five airlines, including American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and United Airlines. Major hubs served include Atlanta, Chicago, and Dallas/Fort Worth, along with leisure destinations like Las Vegas and Orlando.

The airport focuses on convenience and efficiency, featuring shorter lines, free Wi-Fi, and a range of dining and shopping options. The main terminal, which has undergone several expansions since its original construction in 1974, includes a seven-gate concourse and is designed to reflect the local heritage. A significant terminal expansion is currently underway, set to nearly double the airport's size and enhance passenger facilities by spring 2025. ATW supports both commercial and general aviation, providing various services and amenities to ensure a pleasant travel experience.

Broadcom's growth strategy emphasizes strategic acquisitions, allowing it to transition from niche semiconductors to a balanced hardware-software portfolio, positioning it as a leader in intelligent edge computing and AI infrastructure. Cardinal Health, Inc. is a global healthcare services and products company based in Dublin, Ohio. Founded in 1971, it initially operated as a food wholesaler before transitioning to pharmaceutical distribution in the late 1970s. The company has grown significantly through strategic acquisitions, expanding its reach in pharmaceuticals and medical products. It went public in 1983 and officially adopted the name Cardinal Health in 1994.

The company operates in two main segments: Pharmaceutical and Medical. The Pharmaceutical segment focuses on the distribution of branded, generic, and specialty pharmaceuticals, as well as nuclear pharmacy services. The Medical segment includes the manufacturing and distribution of medical and surgical products, laboratory products, and patient recovery solutions. Cardinal Health also offers supply chain solutions and performance analytics to enhance healthcare operations. With approximately 46,500 to 48,000 employees, Cardinal Health serves a diverse network of hospitals, healthcare systems, pharmacies, and laboratories across the U.S. and internationally.

Founded in 1947, the company has grown significantly and now employs over 20,000 people across more than 20 countries. It is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CRL. Charles River provides essential products and services that support the discovery, development, and safe manufacturing of drugs, vaccines, therapeutics, and medical devices.

The company offers a wide range of services, including research models and animal services, safety assessment and toxicology, biologics testing and manufacturing, and discovery and development services. Its expertise spans the entire drug development continuum, from basic research to commercial release. Charles River emphasizes ethical research practices and animal welfare, adhering to the principles of the 3Rs (replacement, reduction, refinement) and adopting new methodologies to enhance research outcomes. Recent digital transformation initiatives have further improved client experiences and accelerated drug development processes.

The company serves a diverse customer base of approximately 2,900 to 5,000 clients across 110 to 130 countries, providing materials that support sectors such as semiconductors, smart devices, and clean energy. Chemours emphasizes sustainable practices and innovation through its global research and development efforts.

Danaher serves a diverse range of sectors, including biopharma, healthcare, and industrial markets, ensuring a strong presence in critical areas of research and development.

Delta Faucet Company is an American manufacturer of plumbing fixtures and materials, based in Indianapolis, Indiana. Founded in 1954 by Alex Manoogian, the company is known for its innovative plumbing solutions, including the first single-handle ball-valve faucet. Delta has expanded its manufacturing capabilities over the years, with facilities in several U.S. states, Canada, and China.

The company offers a diverse range of plumbing products under brands such as Delta, Kraus, Peerless, and Brizo. Their core offerings include various types of faucets, kitchen sinks, bath and shower fixtures, toilets, and water filtration systems. Delta emphasizes water efficiency and user convenience, featuring technologies like DIAMOND valves and Touch2O touch-sensor faucets. Their products are available through wholesalers, plumbers, contractors, and direct-to-consumer channels, catering to both residential and commercial markets.

Eli Lilly and Company is a global research-based pharmaceutical corporation founded in 1876 in Indianapolis, Indiana. Established by Colonel Eli Lilly, the company has grown from a small operation to one of the largest pharmaceutical firms in the world, with products available in approximately 125 countries.

Throughout its history, Eli Lilly has developed numerous significant medications, including the first commercially available insulin product, Iletin®, and the Salk Polio Vaccine, which it was the first to manufacture and distribute globally. The company has also introduced various antibiotics and treatments for conditions like pernicious anemia. In addition to pharmaceuticals, Eli Lilly has diversified into agricultural chemicals, veterinary medicine, cosmetics, and medical instruments. The company is known for its commitment to innovation and humanitarian service, reflecting its founder's vision of continuous improvement.

GM de México is committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences while advancing towards a future of zero emissions, zero crashes, and zero congestion. The company focuses on innovation and sustainability, developing electric and autonomous vehicles powered by the Ultium battery platform. It produces vehicles under well-known brands such as Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac, including the all-electric Cadillac LYRIQ-V and the ESCALADE IQ. 

Additionally, GM de México offers connected vehicle services through OnStar, enhancing safety and customer engagement. The company emphasizes a culture of health, safety, diversity, equity, and inclusion, leveraging its global scale and modernized logistics to support its operations and strategic goals.

High Liner Foods Inc. is a prominent North American processor and marketer of value-added frozen seafood, based in Lunenburg, Nova Scotia. Established in 1899, the company has evolved from its origins in salt fish processing to focus on retail, foodservice, and private-label seafood products. It is publicly traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol HLF.

The company specializes in a variety of frozen seafood items that are easy to prepare, including fish sticks and pan-sear fillets. High Liner's product offerings include well-known retail brands such as High Liner, Fisher Boy, and Sea Cuisine, as well as foodservice brands like Icelandic Seafood and Catch of the Day. High Liner Foods emphasizes sustainability, sourcing nearly 100% of its seafood responsibly and engaging in initiatives to reduce food waste and support hunger relief. The company maintains strong relationships with major supermarket chains, club stores, and foodservice distributors across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

Infrastructure and Energy Alternatives, Inc. (IEA) is a diversified infrastructure construction company based in Indianapolis, Indiana. As a subsidiary of MasTec, Inc., IEA specializes in engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) services across renewable energy, traditional power, and civil infrastructure sectors. Founded in 2011, with roots tracing back to 1974, the company employs around 6,000 people and generates approximately $1.9 billion in revenue. IEA has successfully completed over 200 utility-scale wind and solar projects throughout North America.

IEA operates in two main segments: renewables and specialty civil. In the renewables sector, the company provides full lifecycle support for wind and solar projects. The specialty civil segment includes services such as environmental remediation, rail infrastructure, and heavy civil projects like roads and bridges. IEA offers a range of capabilities, including power delivery, industrial construction, and environmental site management, emphasizing in-house expertise for complex projects.

Kaman Corporation is an aerospace and industrial technology company founded in 1945 by Charles H. Kaman. The company specializes in developing and manufacturing high-tech products, precision components, and technical services for various markets, including government, defense, industrial, commercial, and medical sectors. Headquartered in Bloomfield, Connecticut, Kaman employs over 3,000 people and reported $755 million in revenue in 2023.

Kaman's product offerings include helicopters, rotor blades, and precision-engineered components for aerospace and defense applications. Notable products include the SH-2 Seasprite helicopter and the K-MAX aerial truck. The company also provides repair and replacement parts for industrial applications and has a significant presence in the distribution of parts across various industries. Kaman's services encompass build-to-print manufacturing, custom engineering, and technical services aimed at enhancing efficiency and safety in aviation and industrial operations. With a global reach, Kaman serves customers in over 60 countries, focusing on mission-critical solutions.

Kinder Morgan, Inc. (KMI) is a leading energy infrastructure company in North America, focusing on the transportation, storage, and handling of natural gas, crude oil, refined petroleum products, and carbon dioxide. Founded in 1997 by Richard D. Kinder and William V. Morgan, KMI has grown significantly through strategic acquisitions, including major purchases from companies like Enron and Shell. Land O'Lakes, Inc. is a farmer-owned agricultural cooperative based in Arden Hills, Minnesota, established in 1921. The company operates across various sectors, including dairy foods, crop inputs, animal nutrition, and agricultural sustainability, generating approximately $14 billion in annual sales. It processes around 12 billion pounds of milk each year from about 300,000 agricultural producers, with a membership of nearly 2,000 direct producer-members and 751 member-cooperatives.

The cooperative is known for its diverse product offerings in dairy, including butter, cheese, and specialty items, as well as providing agricultural inputs and services. Land O'Lakes also focuses on animal nutrition, offering products like calf milk replacer and Purina Mills feeds. The company emphasizes innovation and sustainability, contributing to community initiatives through the Land O'Lakes Foundation and supporting global agricultural development via its nonprofit, Venture37. With operations in all 50 U.S. states and over 60 locations worldwide, Land O'Lakes plays a significant role in connecting farmers to consumers.

Magna International Inc. is a global mobility technology company and one of the largest automotive suppliers in the world. Founded in 1957 in Toronto, Canada, it has grown from a small tool and die operation to a major player in the automotive industry, employing approximately 164,000 people across 342 manufacturing operations and 91 product development and engineering centers in 27 countries.

Quincaillerie Richelieu Ltée, also known as Richelieu Hardware Ltd, is a prominent Canadian importer, manufacturer, and distributor of specialty hardware. Founded in 1968 and based in Montreal, Quebec, the company serves over 110,000 customers across North America with a diverse catalog of more than 130,000 products. Richelieu operates 112 distribution centers and two manufacturing plants in Quebec, employing over 3,000 people.

The company specializes in hardware for furniture, cabinetry, and woodworking, offering a wide range of products including decorative and functional hardware, kitchen and closet storage solutions, lighting systems, and high-pressure laminates. Richelieu also produces custom-manufactured items and sells many products under its own brands. Its customer base includes manufacturers and retailers in the residential, commercial, and woodworking sectors, supported by a strong focus on innovation and logistical efficiency.

Rinker Materials is a prominent manufacturer of reinforced concrete infrastructure products based in Houston, Texas. Founded in 1964, the company operates as a QUIKRETE® Company and has over 70 facilities across the United States and Eastern Canada. Rinker employs approximately 453 people and has experienced consistent growth in its workforce.

The company specializes in producing durable and high-strength products, including reinforced concrete pipe, box culverts, and bridge products. These solutions are designed for stormwater management, sanitary sewer systems, and various civil engineering applications. Rinker's products meet or exceed industry standards set by organizations such as ASTM, AASHTO, and AREMA, ensuring reliable performance in demanding environments. Rinker Materials serves municipal, state highway, transportation, and railway infrastructure projects, contributing to essential public works across its operational regions.

Royal Caribbean Group is a leading player in the global vacation industry and the second-largest cruise line operator in the world, based in Miami, Florida. Founded in 1968, the company has grown from a startup to a major force in leisure travel, managing a fleet of 68 ships that sail to around 1,000 destinations worldwide. Its flagship brand, Royal Caribbean International, holds a significant share of the cruise market, making it the largest by revenue.

The company operates several distinct cruise line brands, including Celebrity Cruises and Silversea Cruises, catering to various market segments. Royal Caribbean Group offers a range of vacation experiences, such as cruise vacations with onboard entertainment and dining, land-and-sea cruise tours, and private island destinations like Labadee and CocoCay. The company targets diverse customer segments, including families and adventurous travelers, ensuring a variety of options for different preferences. Its mission focuses on delivering exceptional vacations while fostering innovation and community engagement.

RTX Corporation is an American multinational aerospace and defense conglomerate based in Arlington, Virginia. Formed in 2020 through the merger of United Technologies Corporation's aerospace subsidiaries and Raytheon Company, RTX is one of the largest aerospace and defense manufacturers globally, generating over $68 billion in annual revenue. The company employs more than 185,000 people across its three main business units: Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon.

Collins Aerospace specializes in advanced structures, avionics, and mission systems for both commercial and military aviation. Pratt & Whitney designs and manufactures advanced aircraft engines, including those for military jets. Raytheon focuses on defense systems, providing guided missiles, air defense systems, and various military technologies. RTX serves a diverse range of customers, including the U.S. government and allied nations, and is committed to innovation in areas like artificial intelligence and advanced propulsion. The company emphasizes ethical operations and community impact while investing in research and development to enhance aviation and defense capabilities.

Schneider Electric is a global leader in energy management and automation, based in Rueil-Malmaison, France. Founded in 1836, the company has transitioned from its origins in heavy industry to specialize in electrical distribution, automation, and digital solutions. Key milestones include entering the electricity market in 1891 and rebranding to Schneider Electric after acquiring Lexel in 1999.

The company operates across four main segments: Infrastructure, Industry, Information Technology, and Buildings. It offers a wide range of products and solutions, including medium-voltage equipment, automation systems, uninterruptible power supplies, and building security systems. Schneider Electric is committed to energy efficiency and sustainability, providing services in electrical installation, systems integration, and energy optimization to support various sectors, including data centers, hospitals, and retail. With a rich history of innovation, Schneider Electric continues to lead in energy management and automation solutions globally.

Westmoreland Mining LLC is the oldest independent coal company in the United States, founded in 1854 and headquartered in Lone Tree, Colorado. The company operates as a full-service coal energy provider with operations across the Western United States and Canada. It emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2019 and is now privately held by its former creditors.

The company focuses on sub-bituminous and lignite coal extraction through multiple surface mines, stretching from Alberta, Canada, to San Juan, New Mexico. In 2018, Westmoreland Mining produced 19 million tonnes of coal and has 732 million tonnes in proven and probable reserves. Its operations include a char production facility, a 50% interest in an activated carbon plant, and services related to mining safety and land reclamation. The Rosebud Mine in Montana is one of its significant assets, producing approximately 12 million tons of coal annually. Westmoreland is committed to safety, environmental stewardship, and operational excellence, earning recognition for its efforts in these areas.

Through the ZimVie Institute, the company trains over 100,000 dental professionals annually, supporting their mission to advance clinical technology and improve patient outcomes.

Airgas is a prominent distributor of packaged industrial, medical, and specialty gases, as well as welding and cutting equipment and safety supplies. Founded in 1982, the company has grown significantly through numerous acquisitions and organic development, establishing the largest national distribution network in the U.S. packaged gas industry. In 2016, Airgas became a wholly owned subsidiary of Air Liquide, enhancing its capabilities in serving a diverse range of industries.

The company offers a wide variety of products, including gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, helium, and acetylene, along with related equipment and safety supplies. Airgas also provides bulk and specialty gases for medical and biotechnology applications, as well as welder rentals and machinery leasing for construction, mining, and forestry. With over 230 branches across 31 U.S. states and Canada, Airgas serves a broad customer base, including industrial manufacturing, medical firms, and beverage producers.

Align Technology is a global medical device company founded in 1997, headquartered in San Jose, California. The company specializes in designing and manufacturing invisible orthodontic solutions and digital dental scanning technology. Its flagship product, the Invisalign system, features custom-made clear aligners that straighten teeth using advanced 3D imaging and computer-aided design technology. The Invisalign system includes options tailored for different age groups and treatment complexities.

In addition to the Invisalign system, Align Technology produces iTero intraoral scanners, which enhance orthodontic workflows and patient experiences. The company has established a strong market presence, having trained over ten thousand doctors and expanded its operations internationally. Align Technology has also pursued growth through strategic acquisitions and partnerships, further solidifying its position in the orthodontics market.

American Water is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States, with a history dating back to 1886. It is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange and is the only water utility in the Dow Jones Utility Average, boasting a market capitalization of around $30 billion.

The company provides safe and reliable drinking water and wastewater services to over 14 million people. It operates through two main segments: its regulated business, which manages more than 500 water and wastewater systems across 14 states, and its Military Services Group, which holds long-term contracts with the Department of Defense for water and wastewater systems on military installations. Headquartered in Camden, New Jersey, American Water employs approximately 6,700 professionals and serves both residential and business customers, as well as performing contract operations for municipalities.

The company is dedicated to discovering, developing, and commercializing innovative cancer therapies. Its flagship product, CABOMETYX (cabozantinib), is a small-molecule inhibitor that has gained approval for multiple cancer indications, including renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma. Exelixis also offers COMETRIQ (cabozantinib) for metastatic medullary thyroid cancer and COTELLIC (cobimetinib), developed in partnership for commercialization.

The company has evolved from its origins in functional genomics to a multi-platform oncology firm, utilizing small molecules, biotherapeutics, and antibody-drug conjugates to tackle challenging cancers. Exelixis emphasizes patient-centric innovation and reinvests revenues from CABOMETYX into expanding its pipeline of targeted cancer therapies. The company collaborates with leading pharmaceutical partners to enhance research and market reach, ensuring its therapies are accessible to patients worldwide.

Generac emphasizes sustainability, employee empowerment, and continuous improvement in its operations, adapting its technology to meet diverse regional needs.

Knoll's dedication to sustainable design and adaptation to evolving trends has solidified its position in the furniture industry.

The company operates as a brand owner and manager, emphasizing design, sourcing, and marketing while utilizing strategic licensing for expansion. PVH's operations are supported by a sophisticated supply chain and a commitment to innovation and consumer engagement.

UGI Corporation is a diversified energy distribution company based in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, with operations in the United States and Europe. Founded in 1882, UGI is recognized as the first public utility holding company in the U.S. The company has a rich history marked by significant mergers and acquisitions, including the establishment of AmeriGas, the largest propane marketer in the country.

UGI provides a range of services in the energy sector. It specializes in natural gas distribution, offering transmission, distribution, and storage services, particularly in the Marcellus Shale region. The company also markets propane through its AmeriGas subsidiary and operates in Europe with brands like AvantiGas and Antargaz. Additionally, UGI Energy Services delivers deregulated energy marketing services to commercial and industrial clients, while its renewable natural gas initiatives are supported by subsidiaries such as GHI Energy LLC.

Repair Solutions focuses on aftermarket tools and diagnostic equipment for vehicle mechanics, while Environmental & Fueling Solutions offers monitoring and fueling equipment. Vontier serves a diverse range of customers, including fueling operators, convenience stores, and fleet owners across multiple regions worldwide. The company is committed to innovation in software and sustainability, supported by its Vontier Business System for growth.

Under the leadership of Adolphus Busch, it became the largest brewer in the U.S. by 1901.

The company has also expanded into various non-beer ventures, including aluminum recycling, real estate development, and theme parks like SeaWorld. With a global reach, Anheuser-Busch has evolved from its St. Louis roots to distribute its products worldwide.

Apogee Electronics, based in Santa Monica, California, was founded in 1985 and specializes in high-end digital audio converters, interfaces, and related hardware. The company is known for setting industry standards in sound quality for professional recording and music production. Apogee's innovations, such as anti-aliasing filters and low-jitter clocks, have significantly improved digital audio quality, making it warmer and more analog-like.

The company has a rich history of milestones, including the launch of its first outboard A-D/D-A converters and the introduction of the AD8000, a multichannel 24-bit interface. Its products are widely used in recording studios and by music professionals globally, emphasizing ultimate sound quality and ongoing innovation. Apogee is a women-owned business, led by co-founder and CEO Betty Bennett.

CHS Inc. is a prominent farmer-owned global agribusiness cooperative based in Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota. With roots dating back to the 1920s and 1930s, it was officially formed through the merger of Cenex Inc. and Harvest States Cooperatives in 1998, and rebranded as CHS Inc. in 2003. The cooperative is owned by around 325,000 farmer, rancher, and local cooperative members, primarily in the Midwest and Northwest U.S., and operates in over 450 communities across 16 states, employing approximately 10,730 people.

CHS provides a wide range of integrated solutions in agriculture and energy. It handles over two billion bushels of grains and oilseeds annually, serving as a major buyer and trader. The company also offers agronomy services, including fertilizers and crop inputs, and operates refineries that produce various petroleum products. Additionally, CHS is involved in food processing, producing edible oils and flour through joint ventures. The cooperative emphasizes strategic growth and innovation, including the recent opening of a Crop Science Research Development Center in Minnesota for year-round product testing.

Founded in 1951 in Calgary, Alberta, the company has grown into a multinational operation headquartered in Brampton, Ontario. With over 1,000 employees and approximately $1.5 billion in annual revenue, IKO operates more than 35 plants across North America and Europe, emphasizing vertical integration to ensure product quality and supply chain efficiency.

IKO specializes in asphalt-based roofing solutions, including residential roofing shingles, commercial roofing systems, and waterproofing and insulation materials. IKO also supports roofing contractors with operational tools and innovative systems designed for durability and efficiency. The company distributes its products across all 50 U.S. states, 10 Canadian provinces, and over 40 countries, maintaining a legacy of craftsmanship that spans over 70 years.

Praxair, Inc. was a prominent player in the industrial gases sector, tracing its origins back to 1907. Initially founded as Linde Air Products Company, it became known for producing oxygen from air using cryogenic processes. Over the years, Praxair expanded its operations through various acquisitions, enhancing its global presence and product offerings, including oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide.

In 2018, Praxair merged with Linde AG to form Linde plc, the largest industrial gases company worldwide. This merger combined Praxair's strengths in the Americas with Linde's engineering capabilities across Europe, Africa, and the Middle East. Today, Linde plc serves approximately 2 million customers in over 100 countries, providing a wide range of industrial gases and innovative technologies to support industries such as petrochemicals, healthcare, and food and beverage.

Founded in 1913, the company has a rich history that began as a coal sales brokerage. NACC emphasizes customer service, innovation, integrity, and respect in its operations, supported by various subsidiaries that enhance its mining and resource management capabilities.

Founded in 1923, the company has evolved from its origins in textiles to become a leader in aviation, defense, industrial products, and finance. The company operates through various subsidiaries and brands. In aviation, it includes Textron Aviation, which features Beechcraft and Cessna, and Bell Textron, known for helicopters. In defense, Textron Systems provides advanced weapon systems and unmanned aircraft. The industrial sector includes brands like Kautex and E-Z-GO, while its finance division offers integrated solutions to support its operations. Textron is committed to innovation, having achieved significant milestones in parachute and helicopter technology.

TTI emphasizes innovation and sustainability while maintaining a commitment to operational excellence.

The United States Army is the oldest branch of the U.S. military, established on June 14, 1775. It began as the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War and has grown into a leading land-based fighting force. The Army's mission is to deploy, fight, and win the nation's wars, ensuring land dominance across various conflicts. It operates under civilian control, with the president serving as the commander in chief.

The Army has a rich history, participating in significant conflicts from the Revolutionary War to modern operations in Iraq and Afghanistan. Its core responsibilities include recruiting, training, and equipping soldiers, providing logistics support, and defending U.S. interests globally. The Army also engages in multinational exercises and supports civil authorities during emergencies. Key training institutions include the United States Military Academy at West Point, which prepares future leaders.

UGI Corporation is a diversified energy distribution company based in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, with operations in the United States and Europe. Founded in 1882, UGI is recognized as the first public utility holding company in the U.S. The company has a rich history marked by significant mergers and acquisitions, including the establishment of AmeriGas, the largest propane marketer in the country.

UGI provides a range of services in the energy sector. It specializes in natural gas distribution, offering transmission, distribution, and storage services, particularly in the Marcellus Shale region. The company also markets propane through its AmeriGas subsidiary and operates in Europe with brands like AvantiGas and Antargaz. Additionally, UGI Energy Services delivers deregulated energy marketing services to commercial and industrial clients, while its renewable natural gas initiatives are supported by subsidiaries such as GHI Energy LLC.

Canfor Corporation is a Vancouver-based integrated forest products company, established in 1938. It began as a small mill focused on veneers and has grown into a global leader in sustainable wood products. The company underwent several name changes, becoming Canfor Corporation in 1983 when it went public. It has expanded through acquisitions, including Northwood Inc. and a significant stake in Sweden's Vida Group.

Canfor operates in two main segments: Lumber and Pulp & Paper. The Lumber segment produces a variety of wood products, including lumber, wood chips, and pellets, with an annual capacity of 5.9 billion board feet. The Pulp & Paper segment manufactures various types of pulp and kraft paper, contributing to a total production of 1.1 million tonnes of northern bleached softwood kraft pulp. Headquartered in British Columbia, Canfor has facilities across Canada, the United States, and Sweden, employing over 6,000 people and focusing on sustainability and community partnerships.

Churchill Downs Racetrack combines traditional racing with modern entertainment to meet the needs of its audience.

The company is distinguished by its long-standing record of annual dividend increases, holding the title for the longest consecutive record in the REIT industry at 58 years.

Costco Wholesale Corporation is a publicly traded, membership-based warehouse club retailer and the third-largest retailer in the world. With over 920 locations and more than 145 million cardholders, Costco generates annual revenue exceeding $269.9 billion. The company is headquartered in Issaquah, Washington.

Founded in 1983 by Jim Sinegal and Jeff Brotman, Costco operates on a membership model that offers low prices on a wide range of brand-name products, including food, pharmacy services, and e-commerce options. The company also features its own house label brand, Kirkland Signature. Costco serves both business members and individual consumers, making it a popular choice for diverse shopping needs. In October 2023, Ron Vachris took over as CEO, succeeding Craig Jelinek.

Cox Automotive also provides dealer software, digital marketing tools, and financing options through NextGear Capital. With a strong focus on data-driven innovation, the company aims to transform how vehicles are bought, sold, owned, and used, facilitating significant transaction volumes in the automotive industry.

Today, Graham Packaging produces over 16 billion container units annually from nearly 70 plants across North America, Europe, Asia, and South America.

The company specializes in custom, value-added, and sustainable packaging solutions, offering a wide range of products including bottles, jars, tubes, and canisters. Graham Packaging also operates Graham Recycling, the first bottle-to-bottle recycling facility, which transforms used bottles into resin pellets for new products. Serving various industries such as automotive, beverage, food, and home care, Graham Packaging collaborates with both Fortune 500 companies and small businesses. Headquartered in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, the company employs around 3,316 people and generates annual revenue of $1.4 billion.

The company designs and manufactures flooring solutions for residential, commercial, and institutional use. The company reaches customers through retail stores, home improvement centers, specialty dealers, and direct commercial channels.

The company serves about 6 million retail customers, having expanded its reach through the acquisition of Direct Energy.

Founded in 1925 in Hartford, Connecticut, the company has a rich history of innovation, beginning with its first engine, the R-1340 Wasp. Over the decades, Pratt & Whitney has played a significant role in aviation, producing engines that powered both military and commercial aircraft, particularly during World War II and the post-war era.

The company also offers comprehensive engine lifecycle support, including maintenance and upgrades. As part of RTX, Pratt & Whitney continues to focus on innovation in propulsion systems, contributing to the aerospace industry's growth and development.

GFL serves a diverse clientele, including municipal, residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional customers across North America.

Domtar is a prominent North American manufacturer specializing in pulp, paper, and packaging products. The company has a rich history dating back to 1820, evolving through various predecessor companies. In 2021, Domtar was acquired by Paper Excellence Group, further solidifying its position in the forest products industry.

With corporate offices in Fort Mill, South Carolina, and Montreal, Quebec, Domtar continues to focus on innovation and community support as it serves diverse markets globally.

Sandia National Laboratories (SNL) is a key research and development laboratory under the U.S. Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration. Established in 1949, Sandia focuses on advancing national security through various science-based technologies. It is managed by National Technology and Engineering Solutions of Sandia, a subsidiary of Honeywell International, and is headquartered at Kirtland Air Force Base in Albuquerque, New Mexico, with additional facilities in Livermore, California, and Waimea, Hawaii.

Originally part of the Manhattan Project, Sandia's core mission involves designing, testing, and assembling non-nuclear components of nuclear weapons. The laboratory has broadened its scope to include around 70 areas of activity, such as nuclear deterrence, climate change research, cybersecurity, and energy development. Sandia has made significant contributions to national security through various technologies, including shock-resistant components, satellite detection systems, and advanced detection devices for biological threats. Its mission continues to evolve, reflecting the changing landscape of national security needs.

Tektronix has a rich history of innovation, holding over 3,200 U.S. patents and receiving multiple Emmy Awards for its contributions to broadcasting technology.

The organization operates five hospitals, two satellite emergency departments, and over 40 ambulatory surgery centers, along with more than 400 care sites across Burlington, Camden, and Gloucester counties. Virtua offers a wide range of services, including cardiology, orthopedics, advanced surgery, and maternity care. It also emphasizes community health initiatives, such as mobile screenings and health equity programs. With a workforce of around 14,000 and nearly 3,000 affiliated clinicians, Virtua is recognized for its commitment to quality care and operational efficiency.

W. P. Carey Inc. is a prominent real estate investment trust (REIT) founded in 1973, based in New York City. The company specializes in net lease investments, focusing on sale-leaseback transactions and build-to-suit financing for single-tenant commercial properties. W. P. Carey provides customized capital solutions to a variety of clients, including publicly-traded and privately-held companies, developers, and private-equity firms. Their business model emphasizes long-term, stable income through triple net leases, where tenants cover most property expenses.

As of December 31, 2024, W. P. Carey owns 1,555 properties totaling 183 million square feet across 26 countries, leased to 355 tenants. The company has a significant presence in the U.S., generating approximately 61% of its revenue domestically, while 33% comes from Europe. W. P. Carey has a history of innovation in the real estate sector, having pioneered sale-leaseback financing and expanded its portfolio to include high-quality net lease assets. The company is committed to corporate citizenship, operating under the principle of "Doing Good While Doing Well®."

Barrick aims to be the most valued gold and copper mining business by leveraging its strong assets and skilled workforce.

Blattner is committed to delivering innovative and resilient construction solutions that support the clean energy transition.

With a strong commitment to sustainability, the company aims to reduce waste and promote long-term water quality while serving consumers through diverse channels.

Starting as a single grain warehouse in Iowa, it has grown to become the largest private company in the United States by revenue, operating in approximately 70 countries with around 160,000 employees. Cargill serves 125 markets and focuses on food security through its extensive supply chain connections.

The company offers a diverse range of products and services across agriculture, food production, and commodities trading. Cargill also provides food ingredients, including starches, vegetable oils, and cocoa, along with other services like flour milling and energy trading. With a commitment to research-driven advancements, Cargill connects farmers to markets through a network of warehouses, ports, and trading offices worldwide.

Celanese operates a dual-engine model with global production sites, emphasizing cost leadership through vertical integration in the acetyl chain and a diverse portfolio of specialty materials.

Columbia Sportswear Company is a leading global brand in outdoor and active lifestyle apparel, footwear, accessories, and equipment. Founded in 1938 in Portland, Oregon, and headquartered in Cedar Mill, Washington, the company has a rich history that began as the Columbia Hat Company. It transitioned to sportswear in the 1960s and officially became Columbia Sportswear Company in 1960. The company has remained family-led for generations and has achieved significant milestones, including going public in 1998.

Columbia specializes in durable outdoor apparel, particularly jackets made with breathable waterproof fabrics, and offers a wide range of products for activities such as hiking, snow sports, and fishing. Notable innovations include proprietary technologies like Omni-Heat™ and Omni-Grip™. Columbia also owns several brands, including Sorel and Mountain Hardwear, and targets outdoor enthusiasts with its high-quality gear. The company has sponsored various athletic teams, including freestyle ski teams at the Winter Olympics, reinforcing its commitment to supporting athletes in challenging environments.

Conagra Brands is a diversified food company with a wide range of brands found in nearly every American household. Founded in 1919 in Grand Island, Nebraska, the company has evolved from a regional milling operation to a global food corporation. It became publicly traded in 1942 and has since expanded significantly through acquisitions, including over one hundred prepared food brands.

The company offers a variety of well-known food brands, such as Orville Redenbacher's popcorn, Marie Callender's frozen meals, Slim Jim snacks, Reddi-wip whipped cream, Hebrew National sausages, Bird's Eye frozen vegetables, Gardein plant-based foods, and Duncan Hines cake mixes. Conagra focuses on consumer brands and value-added products, serving both retail and foodservice channels primarily in North America.

CVS Health Corporation is a leading American healthcare company headquartered in the U.S. It ranks as the world's second-largest healthcare company, following UnitedHealth Group. Founded in 1963 in Lowell, Massachusetts, CVS Health operates several well-known brands, including CVS Pharmacy, CVS Caremark, and Aetna. The company has evolved from a discount health and beauty retailer to a comprehensive healthcare provider.

CVS Health offers a wide range of services and products, including a vast retail pharmacy chain that sells health and beauty items, prescription drugs, and over-the-counter products. The company also manages pharmacy benefits through CVS Caremark and provides health insurance services via Aetna. Additionally, CVS Health operates MinuteClinics, which offer in-store healthcare services for common illnesses. The company has grown significantly through strategic acquisitions, expanding its reach and capabilities in the healthcare sector.

Energy Harbor Corp. is an independent power producer and integrated retail energy provider based in Akron, Ohio. Founded in 2019, the company specializes in carbon-free and green electricity plans for residential, commercial, and industrial customers across Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia. Energy Harbor operates a fleet of nuclear and fossil fuel generators, producing around 30 million megawatt-hours annually and serving nearly one million customers.

The company focuses on safety, reliability, and sustainability, offering fixed-price energy plans to protect customers from market fluctuations. Energy Harbor emphasizes environmental protection through its commitment to carbon-free power. It provides retail energy supply, power generation, energy trading, and customer support services. In March 2024, Energy Harbor was acquired by Vistra Corp., enhancing its operations and expanding its nuclear generation capacity.

Gilead Sciences, Inc. is a biopharmaceutical company based in Foster City, California, founded in 1987. The company focuses on discovering, developing, and commercializing innovative medicines for viral diseases, HIV, hepatitis, oncology, and other serious health conditions. Gilead has a strong history of research and development, with significant milestones including the FDA approval of its first product, Vistide, in 1996, and the introduction of groundbreaking HIV treatments like Viread and the first single-tablet regimen.

Gilead's product portfolio includes a range of antiviral medications and therapies for various conditions. The company has expanded its reach through strategic acquisitions, such as Kite Pharma for cell therapy, and has established community initiatives to support patients, including the COMPASS Initiative and HepConnect. With a global presence in over 20 countries and a commitment to addressing unmet medical needs, Gilead continues to advance healthcare solutions for patients worldwide.

The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, founded in 1898 in Akron, Ohio, is a global leader in tire manufacturing and rubber products. With around 66,000 employees across 48 facilities in 21 countries, Goodyear has a rich history of innovation in tire technology. The company began by producing bicycle and carriage tires and quickly expanded into automobile tires, becoming the world's largest rubber company by 1926.

Goodyear's core products include tires for automobiles, bicycles, aircraft, and racing. The company has introduced several key innovations, such as the first tubeless automobile tire in 1903 and the first synthetic rubber tire in 1937. Goodyear also operates innovation centers focused on research and development for advanced tire technology. Over the years, it has formed partnerships and subsidiaries, including Kelly Tires and Dunlop, and has made significant contributions to motorsports and wartime aircraft production.

Greystar is committed to enriching the lives of residents, property owners, and investors through its comprehensive services.

Hiland Dairy Foods Company, established in 1938 in Springfield, Missouri, is a prominent farmer-owned dairy processor and distributor. With a history that includes expansions and acquisitions, the company operates 19 plants and 64 distribution centers across 10 states, including Arkansas, Iowa, and Texas. Under the leadership of President Aggus, appointed in 2023, Hiland employs nearly 4,000 people and generates around $2 billion in sales, focusing on delivering fresh dairy products from local farmer-owners within 48 hours.

Hiland offers a diverse range of dairy products, such as milk (including flavored varieties), butter, ice cream, cottage cheese, yogurt, and cheese, as well as non-dairy beverages like orange juice and tea. The company maintains high quality standards and has received multiple awards for its products. Hiland has a strong commitment to community engagement, supporting local grocery stores and participating in charitable events, reinforcing its ties to the regions it serves.

Founded in 1898 through the merger of 17 pulp and paper mills, the company is headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee, and employs approximately 39,000 people. The company primarily focuses on two business segments: Industrial Packaging, which accounts for about 70% of its revenue, and Global Cellulose Fibers. IP produces a variety of products, including containerboard, corrugated packaging, specialty pulps, and fiber-based products for various industries. With a commitment to sustainability and innovation, IP manages around 23 million hectares of forestland and emphasizes environmentally friendly packaging solutions. The company reported $18.62 billion in revenue for 2024, reflecting its strong market position and ongoing growth.

Short Description: The City of Roseburg is a growing, vital community which enjoys a high quality of life in a semi-rural setting.  Roseburg is located in the beautiful "Heart of the Land of Umpqua" region in southwestern Oregon.  The elevation is 465 feet, and features a mild, fair seasonal climate.  Average rainfall is 30.7 inches with occasional light snow.  Average summer temperature is 78 with a few days up to 100.  Average winter temperature is 44.67 with a few days in the low 30s or 20s.  Roseburg is the county seat and largest city in Douglas County.  The population is 24,820 with an urban daytime population of approximately 60,000.  Roseburg is the hub of retail, government activity and medical services for Central Douglas County.  The City is served by Roseburg School District #4, which has an excellent reputation and community support.  Umpqua Community College is 5 miles north of the City and offers a varied curriculum with extensive adult education and community oriented classes.  Multiple locations at the college are available for cultural activities, and there is a thriving community theater group with its own venue in a city park.  The city boasts numerous park areas, including tennis courts, soccer and ball fields, a 9-hole golf course, skate park, disc golf course, dog park and walking trails.  Roseburg is the location of choice for many who seek a high quality living environment at a reasonable price.  Various community events, including Graffiti Week, Art and Wine Festivals and Music on the Half Shell, among others, are held throughout the year for local residents and tourists.  There are numerous shopping opportunities from specialty shops in historic downtown to nationwide chain stores.  Roseburg's economy has diversified in recent years while still retaining strong ties to its natural resource base.  Efforts to bring clean industries and new jobs to the area have been fruitful and are continuing through support by a coalition of government agencies and funding.

Its commitment to innovation is reflected in its recent strategic acquisitions and the development of digitally integrated platforms for environmental compliance and enterprise management.

Trimble Inc. is a global technology company founded in 1978, headquartered in Westminster, Colorado. It specializes in providing hardware, software, and services that connect the physical and digital worlds across various industries, including construction, agriculture, geospatial, and transportation. Trimble pioneered commercial GPS technology and has a rich history of innovation, including the launch of the first GPS receiver in 1984 and advancements in real-time kinematic GPS.

The company offers integrated solutions that leverage GPS, GNSS, and positioning technologies. Its products and services include geospatial and surveying tools, construction and infrastructure solutions, and precision agriculture technologies. Trimble has established partnerships with notable companies like Caterpillar and Nikon, enhancing its offerings in construction and infrastructure. With operations in over 30 countries, Trimble emphasizes innovation, sustainability, and community impact through its initiatives.

Its portfolio includes four well-known brands: KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell, and The Habit Burger Grill, each catering to different market segments.

The company focuses on sustainable growth and aims to expand its beloved restaurant brands while adapting to local tastes and preferences.

AltaGas Ltd. is a prominent North American energy infrastructure company based in Calgary, Alberta. Founded in 1994, it connects natural gas, natural gas liquids, and energy markets across Canada and the United States. The company employs around 3,000 people and manages over $21 billion in assets.

AltaGas operates through two main segments: Utilities and Midstream, along with power generation capabilities. The Utilities segment serves approximately 1.6 to 1.8 million customers in several U.S. states, providing regulated natural gas distribution and storage services. The Midstream segment focuses on the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, handling significant volumes of natural gas and offering services such as processing, transportation, and export logistics. Additionally, AltaGas operates gas-fired power generation assets with a capacity of 508 megawatts, primarily located in California. The company emphasizes integrated infrastructure and collaborates with Indigenous and community groups to enhance safety and environmental performance.

Arconic Corporation, based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, specializes in advanced aluminum products. Established on April 1, 2020, following a separation from Arconic Inc., the company has roots dating back to 1888. It reported $7.3 billion in revenue in 2019 and is publicly traded on the NYSE under the ticker ARNC.

The company focuses on aluminum sheet, plate, extrusions, and innovative architectural products. Its markets include aerospace, automotive, industrial applications, packaging, and commercial building and construction. Arconic is recognized for its engineering solutions and operates a global network of production facilities, including key sites in Davenport, Iowa, and Samara, Russia. The company also has a dedicated R&D center in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and supports workforce development through the Arconic Foundation. 

Arconic's product offerings include aluminum solutions for aerospace and automotive applications, advanced brazing sheets for thermal management, and comprehensive building façade products. Its commitment to quality and efficiency positions it as a leader in the aluminum industry.

Founded in 1908, the company has a rich history of innovation, starting with early ventures into automotive parts and evolving into a leader in engine manufacturing. It gained prominence with the introduction of the Type “P” one-horsepower engine in 1920 and has continued to develop advanced engine technologies, including lightweight aluminum engines and fuel-efficient models.

The company specializes in engines that power a variety of applications, such as lawn mowers, snow blowers, garden tractors, and generators. Briggs & Stratton also produces racing engines and gear through its Motorsports Division. With a commitment to sustainability, the company manufactures engines from 98% recycled aluminum. It serves a global market, providing products to mass retailers and various sectors, including agriculture and powersports.

Brasfield & Gorrie, LLC is a national general contracting firm based in Birmingham, Alabama, founded in 1964. The company specializes in construction management, design-build, and general contracting services across various sectors, including healthcare, commercial, institutional, federal, municipal, industrial, and infrastructure projects. With a workforce of over 3,700 employees, Brasfield & Gorrie operates 13 offices across eight states and has completed projects in 39 states.

The firm is known for its comprehensive construction solutions, including general contracting for complex projects, construction management at risk, and design-build services. It has a strong reputation in healthcare construction and has pioneered expertise in concrete structures and sustainable building practices, achieving LEED Silver certification for notable projects. Some of its landmark projects include the Georgia Dome, the AT&T Building in Nashville, and various government and educational facilities. The company emphasizes a people-first culture, community involvement, and a commitment to safety and quality craftsmanship.

Keith Oden, among others. Camden trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CPT.

The company has a rich history, having established a strong partnership with McDonald's in the 1950s, which helped pioneer one-stop shopping for quick-service restaurants.

Their offerings include fresh and cooked meat products, liquid condiments like ketchup and syrups, dairy and produce, and bakery operations. They also provide comprehensive distribution and logistics services, serving over 25,000 restaurants globally, including well-known brands like Starbucks, Chick-Fil-A, and Taco Bell. GSF is committed to quality and customer satisfaction, guided by core values that emphasize fairness, product excellence, and high standards.

The company specializes in sterilization, infection prevention, and surgical products for healthcare, pharmaceuticals, and other sectors. The company offers a wide range of products and services, including sterilization technologies, surgical equipment, and infection prevention solutions. Their portfolio features low-temperature liquid chemical systems, steam and gas sterilizers, surgical tables and lights, and various disinfectants. STERIS serves a diverse clientele, primarily focusing on hospitals, surgical centers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers, emphasizing innovation in infection control and safety across multiple industries.

Taylor Morrison Home Corporation is one of the largest homebuilders and developers in the United States, based in Scottsdale, Arizona. Formed in 2007 through the merger of Taylor Woodrow and Morrison Homes, the company has a legacy that spans over a century. It operates in 12 states and 20 markets, focusing on mid-to-upscale housing as well as homes for first-time and mid-market buyers.

The company builds single-family and multifamily detached homes under various brand offerings, including Taylor Morrison, Esplanade, and Yardly. In addition to homebuilding, Taylor Morrison provides financial services such as mortgage financing, title insurance, and homeowners' insurance. The company serves a diverse range of customers, from entry-level homebuyers to luxury buyers and those seeking resort-style living. Taylor Morrison has been recognized as "America's Most Trusted® Builder" for ten consecutive years, highlighting its commitment to quality and customer satisfaction.
